title: Tech Note: Backup Settings for Distributed Applications
author: Jean-Yves Fock-Hoon, QA Manager, 4D Inc.
featured_technology: 4D Backup system and Backup.XML project file
PROCESS HTML TAGS command for XML templating
On Startup / On Server Startup database methods
Get 4D folder / Test path name commands

historical_commentary.text: This note addresses a genuinely recurring pain point for distributed 4D applications of its era: a Backup.XML project file baked in at development time containing a stale local backup destination path, which forces an unwanted folder-selection dialog once the application is moved to a new machine. Its proposed solution — a Backup.XML2 template processed at startup with PROCESS HTML TAGS rather than hard-coded DOM/XML-building code — is a clever, still-instructive templating pattern, though it depends entirely on 4D Backup's classic XML project file format and the companion 4D Backup product from that generation, both of which should be re-verified against current 4D Backup/4D Server behavior before reuse.
related_updates: 4D Backup's project file format and startup behavior are specific to this generation of 4D (v2004) and should be re-checked against current 4D Server/Backup documentation before applying this technique

4D Backup, 4D Write, 4D View, and similar companion products from this era have themselves evolved considerably (e.g., 4D Write Pro launched in 2016, 4D View Pro in 2018), and backup/preferences handling in modern 4D may differ from what is described here
